# OmniGauge

> One terminal dashboard for every AI plan you pay for. Reads Claude Code,
> OpenAI Codex and Grok CLI usage from files those tools already write to your
> disk, normalises four incompatible counters onto one denominator, and shows
> plan quota, token volume, burn rate and time-to-reset side by side.

This file exists because the site is a terminal UI rendered in JavaScript. The
page is roughly 49KB, of which about 1KB is crawlable text — so anything that
does not execute scripts sees almost none of it. Everything below is the same
content, in plain text.

## The problem

Every vendor reports usage honestly and incomparably.

- Codex counts **down** — "38% left" — on a 5-hour rolling window
- Claude counts **up** — "87% used" — on a calendar week
- Grok gives **raw tokens** against a monthly cap
- Gemini says **"limited"** and gives no number at all

Four tabs and some mental arithmetic later you still do not know which plan runs
out first. OmniGauge inverts what needs inverting, converts raw counts to
percentages, states every window in the same terms, and puts them on one axis.
The answer is usually not the plan you were worried about.

## What it does

- **Plan quota** — every provider on one scale: used, remaining, when it resets
- **Token volume** — from local transcripts, with per-model attribution
- **Burn rate and exhaustion forecast** — tokens per hour, and when you run dry
- **Lifetime totals** — including models you no longer use
- **Alerts** — `--check` exits 0/1/2 so cron can act on it
- **Live view** — `--watch` refreshes in place

## What it refuses to do

- **No keys for the part that matters.** Plan quota and token volume come from
  files your agents already write to your own disk, and from each CLI's own
  quota panel. Nothing to configure, nothing to paste, nothing to leak.
- **API dollar spend is optional and does need a key** for whichever vendor you
  want it from. That key is stored at 0600, never passed as a command-line
  argument, and the file is refused outright if it is group- or world-readable.
  Leave spend off and no credential — and no network call — is involved at all.
- **No telemetry.** No account, no server, no phone-home. Your consumption is
  nobody's business.
- **No guessing.** When a vendor changes its UI and a parse fails you get
  `NO QUOTA PARSED` and the raw screen — never a plausible number with nothing
  behind it. A dashboard that invents a figure is worse than one that admits it
  is blind.
- **No dependencies.** One Python file, 3.8+, stdlib only. `tmux` is needed only
  for quota scraping.

## Install

```
git clone https://github.com/omnigauge/omnigauge.git
install -m755 omnigauge/omnigauge ~/.local/bin/omnigauge
omnigauge --refresh
```

Then `omnigauge` for the board, `--doctor` for what is connected, `--watch` to
follow it live, `--check` for cron, `--since 7d` for any window.

## Adding a provider

A provider is one file in `providers/`. It answers four questions: are you
installed, where are your files, how many tokens, and what does your quota panel
say. `providers/claude.py` is the worked example. Pull requests are open to
anyone — no permission needed.

Three rules that are not style preferences: report **percent used** always,
inverting vendors that report remaining; **fail loudly, never plausibly**; and
**never invent a figure the vendor did not give you**.
